Example 24. Consider any positive integers i0, n, k such that i0 < n and k ≥2.
Let w be a
permutation in Sn defined by wi = n+1−i for i ∈[i0 −1] and wi = i−i0 +1 for i ∈{i0, i0 +1, . . . , n}.
This is a special case of a valley permutation, where the increasing part consists of smaller numbers
than the decreasing part. We obtain that the Lehmer code of this permutation is (cw)j = n −i for
each i ∈[i0 −1] and (cw)i = 0 for i ∈{i + 1, i + 2, . . . , n}. Therefore we obtain from Theorem 4.1
